atom.biological_role: L-carnitine accepts and releases fatty-acyl groups in the mitochondrial shuttle, sustaining long-chain fatty-acid entry for oxidation. Dietary L-carnitine supplies this same circulating substrate alongside endogenous synthesis.
atom.evidence_limitation: Functional dependency and food composition support Capacity, not a need to increase intake. Endogenous synthesis, tissue uptake and conservation also sustain the pool. The existing extracted carnitine/carbohydrate intervention is formulation-specific; meat or dairy effects on transport flux, brain function or ADHD are not established.
atom.dietary_input_note: 2026-10-23: authorised Type A Capacity / Direct admission. Provision is distinct from incremental benefit or dietary indispensability.

assessment.operation: Enable long-chain fatty-acid transport into mitochondria so fat-derived ATP production can proceed.

functional_dependency.statement: The shuttle reaction uses L-carnitine to transfer long-chain acyl groups; enzyme-function evidence and versioned reaction annotation establish the PM-specific dependency.

dietary_supply.statement: Directly measured food L-carnitine supplies the same substrate; no conversion from total protein or generalisation of a supplemental effect is used.

assessment.assessment_limitations: Functional dependency and food composition support Capacity, not a need to increase intake. Endogenous synthesis, tissue uptake and conservation also sustain the pool. The existing extracted carnitine/carbohydrate intervention is formulation-specific; meat or dairy effects on transport flux, brain function or ADHD are not established.

targeted_searches.query: Demarquoy radioisotopic free L-carnitine beef lamb dairy food samples; canonical L/(R) identity
targeted_searches.outcome: Primary publisher text explicitly identifies beef/lamb samples. Two qualitative provisional sources; exact preparation/cut unresolved. No kefir or blanket dairy edge created.
